scope: Coverage-guided fuzzing must exercise parsers, storage log replay, userspace image metadata, sync frames, capability messages, and kernel/user ABI decoding before release.
current_evidence: Adversarial spec tests reject malformed manifests, corrupted storage logs, stale metadata, and bypass attempts.

The release-security checker runs deterministic mutation fuzzing from checked seed corpora against binary cursors, userspace descriptors, ELF image metadata, storage volume loading, sync record decoding, capability messages, and syscall ABI range validation, and release-security-check now runs checker unit tests for keyring fail-closed behavior.
graduation_criteria: Keep release-running fuzz harnesses, checked seed corpora, deterministic mutation counts, crash redaction fixtures, and regression tests wired into release-security-check before tagging.
cisa_alignment: Treat exploit-prone input handling as a manufacturer-owned defect class and block release when parser fuzz evidence is absent.

scope: Fault injection must cover boot artifact tamper, rollback failure, service startup, permission review, power loss, torn writes, storage driver crash/rebind, recovery repair, and sync transport disruption.
current_evidence: QEMU smoke paths include service startup, permission review, tampered artifacts, rollback-slot failure, recovery proof, storage durability, sync two-node, and driver restart gates.
Recovery entry now rejects duplicate action lists and zero boot ticks, while break-glass recovery requires bounded single-line audit reasons before recording approval.

The public release-security-gate target aggregates native smoke tamper profiles, storage durability, driver restart, recovery, sync two-node, UEFI QEMU preflight, and the real NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof checker into the release matrix.
graduation_criteria: Keep service startup, permission review, storage, driver, recovery, sync, boot tamper, rollback, UEFI fault campaigns, and the NUC11TNKi5 real-hardware proof bundle in the release matrix with deterministic artifacts and failure triage records.
cisa_alignment: Exercise secure-by-default behavior under failure instead of depending on customer recovery workarounds.

scope: Release artifacts must be buildable from pinned inputs with deterministic outputs or documented, bounded nondeterminism.
current_evidence: The repository pins the Zig toolchain entrypoint and keeps generated artifacts under build outputs.

The reproducible-build-check target copies the Jujutsu working-copy file list into two isolated workspaces, builds release artifacts independently, compares kernel, ISO, signing tool, and userspace image digests, and records repo_vcs=jj, repository, Jujutsu change ID, commit ID, dirty workspace count, toolchain, and result metadata under build/release-security.
graduation_criteria: Keep a reproducible-build release target that performs two isolated Jujutsu source snapshots, compares artifact digests, records repository, Jujutsu source identity, toolchain, and environment metadata, and fails on undocumented nondeterminism.
cisa_alignment: Support supply-chain transparency and reduce unverified build inputs before customer distribution.

scope: Every release artifact must carry machine-readable SBOM data, source provenance, signer identity, measured boot inputs, customer-verifiable digest records, and DSSE-wrapped attestations signed by hardware-backed release keys.
current_evidence: Userspace archives, boot measurements, signed bundle state, and launch provenance are modeled and tested.

The release-sbom-provenance target emits artifact-digests.sha256, artifact-measurements.json, SPDX 2.3 SBOM JSON, in-toto/SLSA provenance statements, DSSE provenance envelopes, release keyring metadata, revocation metadata, customer verification policy, and a disclosure dry-run bundle under build/release-security, with SLSA externalParameters anchored to Jujutsu sourceControl=jj, changeId, commit id, repository, and Zig version; the generator now fails closed before output if required release inputs such as the boot ISO, kernel, release tools, userspace image directory, readiness manifest, keyring, or revocation metadata are missing.

The release generator can delegate every DSSE PAE signing operation to a TPM, secure enclave, HSM, or KMS command through ZIGOS_RELEASE_DSSE_SIGN_COMMAND, keeping release code on key handles instead of seed material; static DSSE signature environment variables are local-preview-only, require an explicit opt-in flag, cannot be combined with signing commands, are rejected whenever hardware-backed release mode is requested, and signer output must be nonempty standard base64 before any DSSE envelope is emitted.

The zigos-verify-release customer CLI validates downloaded artifact digests, DSSE signatures before payload parsing, revoked key ids/generations, active release-key verifier metadata digests, exactly one signed SLSA subject per DSSE envelope plus pinned release-security buildType, pinned builder id, Jujutsu source identity externalParameters, zero dirtyWorkspaceFileCount in signed SLSA run metadata, active key validity windows against signed SLSA runDetails.metadata.startedOn, exact artifact measurement coverage without duplicates, complete reproducible-build digest and source identity evidence with dirty_workspace_file_count=0 that must match the signed SLSA repository/change/commit/toolchain identity, SPDX version metadata, post-quantum keyring policy, and required-mode ML-DSA signature coverage.

The release-security checker rejects release artifact metadata, generator sources, reproducible-build checker sources, customer verifier sources, or keyrings that omit required generator input enforcement, Jujutsu source provenance, DSSE envelopes, hardware-backed key custody, active-key lifecycle dates, configured public keys, verifier metadata digests, provider names, rotation, revocation, customer verifier protocols, artifact measurements, executable verifier tooling, FIPS 203 ML-KEM/FIPS 204 ML-DSA/FIPS 205 SLH-DSA policy, measured rollout, or the explicit statement that ed25519 stays the classical baseline until a validated FIPS 204 ML-DSA provider is linked; release-security-check includes negative keyring fixtures proving public releases fail closed while any required release key remains required-not-configured.
graduation_criteria: Generate SPDX SBOMs plus DSSE-wrapped in-toto/SLSA provenance attestations for kernels, userspace images, tools, policy manifests, and ISO outputs.

Sign each DSSE PAE payload with a hardware-backed TPM, secure enclave, HSM, or KMS release key, publish customer-verifiable keyring and revocation metadata, and fail release if the signing key is missing, stale, or revoked.

Keep zigos-verify-release validating artifact digests, DSSE signatures, exactly one SLSA subject per DSSE envelope, signed SLSA builder identity, signed SLSA Jujutsu source identity, zero dirty workspace evidence, key generation, revocation status, signed SLSA startedOn coverage by key validity windows, exact artifact measurement coverage, complete reproducible-build source evidence that matches signed SLSA identity, post-quantum policy, and required ML-DSA coverage for every public release.
cisa_alignment: Maintain SBOMs and transparent vulnerability/exploitability records for first- and third-party software.

scope: Threat-model tests must cover explicit authority, privilege boundaries, boot trust, recovery, policy mediation, storage integrity, sync trust, diagnostics privacy, and driver isolation.
current_evidence: Spec conformance and adversarial tests already encode revoked capability, expired lease, malformed manifest, corrupted log, rollback, bypass, hidden observability, and unsupported continuous process-observation threats.

The kernel capability table now stores live capabilities and target revocation generations in indexed arenas with holder and target multimap indexes, so authority lookup, grant rollback, pass/revoke, holder/target queries, and target-generation reservation no longer depend on bespoke fixed-slot free-list scans.

spec/release_security/threat_model.json publishes a reviewer-facing matrix with threat IDs, abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, residual-risk owners, and release decisions for every required security domain.
graduation_criteria: Keep the threat-model matrix release-gated and require every P0/P1 release track to list abuse cases, mitigations, negative tests, and residual-risk decisions.
cisa_alignment: Make security properties measurable across the product lifecycle and prevent dangerous defaults from shipping silently.

scope: Unsafe Zig and kernel-adjacent sections must be inventoried, reviewed, minimized, and bound by tests before release, especially pointer casts, integer-pointer conversion, inline assembly, packed ABI structs, and user memory copies.
current_evidence: The kernel and native syscall paths centralize many low-level boundaries and have targeted negative tests around user memory and brokered devices.

spec/release_security/memory_safety_inventory.json inventories every tracked Zig source file containing pointer conversion, pointer casts, inline assembly, packed or extern ABI structs, volatile access, or atomic primitives, and the release-security checker rejects any new unsafe source path without release-reviewed owner, mitigation, and test coverage.
graduation_criteria: Keep an unsafe-surface inventory, required audit owner, reviewer checklist, and tests for every user-memory copy, pointer conversion, inline assembly block, and kernel allocator invariant.
cisa_alignment: Treat memory-safety roadmaps and migration/mitigation evidence as mandatory for unsafe or kernel-adjacent code.

scope: Crash dumps, event-ledger exports, remote diagnostics, and support bundles must redact secrets, private object names, personal content, capability tokens, and raw memory by default.
current_evidence: Event-ledger, supervisor, and spec tests verify redacted diagnostics for crashes, permission decisions, remote shares, and autonomous agent authorization/action denials.

Crash record summaries now redact sensitive reason text by default, and spec/release_security/crash_dump_redaction.json gates raw memory denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, support-bundle review, and reproducible redaction fixtures.

Hardware-backed secret vault imports now fail closed unless an explicit seal provider is attached; provider use is recorded on sealed records, the secret-vault service and backing store use indexed arenas for secret and handle lookup/allocation, active vault handles are indexed for active-at-tick checks and removed on revoke, and the production-readiness checker rejects software digest fallback for hardware-backed secret claims.

The OS identity passkey store now uses an indexed arena for credential registration and lookup, rejects full credential tables before importing backing secrets, and keeps assertion, recovery, and revocation mutations tracked by credential id.
graduation_criteria: Keep explicit crash dump policy tests for raw memory capture denial, opt-in scoped diagnostics, capability token scrubbing, private object-name scrubbing, and reproducible redaction fixtures.
cisa_alignment: Keep security-sensitive telemetry safe by default and avoid shifting diagnostic privacy risk to customers.

scope: A release must have a published vulnerability disclosure policy, private intake channel, triage SLA, CVE/CWE handling process, coordinated disclosure rules, and security update commitments.
current_evidence: SECURITY.md publishes GitHub private vulnerability reporting and a backup security mailbox, with monitored release-security-review ownership, 3-business-day acknowledgement, 10-business-day triage, coordinated disclosure, CVE/CWE handling, and security update commitments.
spec/release_security/vulnerability_disclosure.json encodes the private intake channels, owner, SLA, CVE/CWE process, and dry-run workflow artifact required by the release gate.
graduation_criteria: Keep the private intake channel published, maintainers on rotation, CVE issuance ownership documented, and end-to-end disclosure dry-run recorded before release.
cisa_alignment: Avoid the CISA bad practice of shipping without a scoped vulnerability disclosure policy and timely CVE/CWE process.

first_hardware_target.selection_reason: Single commodity x86_64 UEFI target with ACPI, integrated display output, USB xHCI input path, M.2 NVMe storage, and wired Intel I225-LM Ethernet so the first hardware proof does not depend on Wi-Fi or dongles.
first_hardware_target.boot_medium: UEFI GRUB ISO or USB image built from build/os.iso.
first_hardware_target.serial_capture: Real-machine serial, framebuffer capture, or HDMI capture logs archived under build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/ as a complete proof bundle and checked by scripts/check-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh.
proof_bundle_requirements: proof-manifest.txt must tie the bundle to intel-nuc11tnki5, NUC11TNKi5, real_hardware, the checked serial.log path, the checked sidecar file paths including attestation-lifecycle.txt, the checked marker contract path, repo_vcs=jj, the Jujutsu change ID, the commit ID, a clean repo_dirty_files=0 state, preparation/capture times with captured_at_utc not before prepared_at_utc, and operator.

serial.log must come from the Intel NUC11TNKi5 and include real-hardware source metadata, exact board SKU metadata, proof-manifest metadata, every required subsystem PASS marker, every concrete hardware fact marker, every booted production-evidence marker, and all minimum cycle counters without duplicate required markers or cycle-counter lines.
proof-manifest.txt, firmware-settings.txt, power-cycle-notes.txt, and attestation-lifecycle.txt must not contain duplicate required keys.

firmware-settings.txt must record BIOS/UEFI version, boot_mode=UEFI, an explicit Secure Boot state of enabled, disabled, or disabled-for-local-proof-media, storage_mode=nvme, wake/suspend settings, and any changed firmware options.

power-cycle-notes.txt must record operator notes, started/completed times with completed_at_utc not before started_at_utc, the ten cold boots, ten warm reboots, one hundred NVMe read/write cycles, one hundred I225-LM frame cycles, twenty suspend/resume cycles, ten induced crash-recovery cycles, ten crash-record persistence checks, and ten update rollback power cycles, and those sidecar counters must exactly match the serial.log counters.

attestation-lifecycle.txt must record the real-hardware provider, root key id, positive initial generation, higher active generation, positive revoked generation count, stale-generation rejection, revoked-generation rejection, stale-attestation verifier rejection, request-bound verifier metadata digest, 64-hex verifier metadata digest, 64-hex attestation request digest, operator, notes, and captured_at_utc not before the proof manifest prepared_at_utc.

artifact-digests.sha256 must contain only well-formed SHA-256 digest rows and record exactly one SHA-256 digest per required ISO or USB image, kernel, userspace service image, release policy artifact, production readiness manifest, release artifact manifest, hardware marker contract, and driver image artifact under the checked artifact root.
scripts/check-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh must pass against the proof bundle directory, not a QEMU or OVMF preflight log.
hardware_exit_criteria: Ten cold UEFI boots and ten warm reboots reach native-ready on the NUC11TNKi5 without panic, hang, or firmware fallback.

ACPI table discovery, APIC timer interrupt proof, GOP framebuffer scanout proof, USB xHCI keyboard input, NVMe read/write, Intel I225-LM transmit/receive, suspend/resume, crash persistence, and update rollback each emit the required hardware target marker plus the corresponding concrete fact marker.

Generated userspace startup, service IPC connectivity, compositor framebuffer presentation, permission review rendering, sync replication/restart, driver restart/rebind, crash-record persistence, and update rollback health checks emit the required booted production-evidence markers.
Twenty suspend/resume cycles preserve timer, framebuffer, USB input, NVMe, and network usability.

Ten induced crash-recovery cycles preserve the native store and produce redacted recovery diagnostics, and ten crash-record persistence checks prove those diagnostics survive reboot without exposing raw memory.
Ten update rollback cycles survive real power transitions and return to the verified active slot without losing persisted state.
Every hardware proof bundle includes a proof manifest, serial output, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, attestation lifecycle evidence, and the exact kernel/userspace artifact digests.
open_gaps: No NUC11TNKi5 serial log has been captured from real hardware yet.

The kernel now preserves the GRUB Multiboot handoff, requests a 32-bit framebuffer, validates memory-map and GOP framebuffer descriptors, scans SMBIOS for the NUC11TNKi5 SKU, and composes early ACPI/MADT/FADT/APIC evidence, but those paths have not been captured from the selected NUC firmware.

Real-device xHCI keyboard input reports, NVMe read/write cycles, Intel I225-LM transmit/receive cycles, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume loops, induced crash-recovery loops, persisted crash-record checks, update rollback power-cycle loops, and booted production-evidence markers still need execution and capture.

tracks.title: Object store and storage volume durability
current_evidence: Content-addressed objects use signed metadata, chunked blob records, and Merkle-addressed payload manifests.

The storage volume can save and replay segmented logs through image-backed and callback-backed attached-volume paths, with generic callbacks and target NVMe PCI attachments represented by distinct backend kinds; direct ATA-device attachment, broker-specific volume backend kinds, and ATA C-bridge exports are retired.

Host tests cover corrupted payload rejection, malformed root-log metadata, torn-record rejection, compaction, page-sized payload reload, undersized image rejection without state mutation, power-loss before root commit, partial-sector log corruption fallback, long-running replay/compaction gates, indexed workspace/snapshot replay, production storage attachment-kind separation, and shared-memory transfer into the storage service.

Workspace share grants now keep a resident principal index rebuilt with workspace state, workspace path indexes maintain object-id slots, workspace and snapshot arenas expose resident counts and indexed snapshot-id lookup, workspaces cache the oldest live snapshot generation for mutation-log compaction guards, and the object store tracks the latest inserted version id, max blob payload bytes, and object-type buckets, so object access, any-access, reshare policy checks, object-to-path share resolution, latest-version retrieval, type-scoped object queries, snapshot existence checks, dirty-snapshot persistence, compaction safety checks, and quota payload usage use keyed or cached lookups instead of scanning storage tables.
The first supported storage envelope is exported from storage_volume.first_supported_capacity_envelope and checked before image or attached-volume persistence.

Writes that exceed the first supported envelope have an explicit user-facing quota policy: reject without partial persistence, report storage.quota.* limit codes, surface NoSpaceLeft at the persistence gate, and reject undersized demo images instead of carrying migration paths; attached-volume production persistence and native-store root adoption require a capacity-checked NVMe PCI backend rather than generic callback or ATA bootstrap backends.

Native-store QEMU helpers attach persistence images as NVMe controllers only, including storage durability and two-node sync boots, while benchmark thresholds now gate segmented replay and forced checkpoint compaction.
capacity_envelope: Volume image: 786432 bytes across 1536 required device sectors, with 785408 bytes available for replay logs.
Object store: 192 objects, 768 versions, 640 blobs, 224 chunks, 28 chunks per payload, 4096-byte chunks, and a 114688-byte maximum object payload.
Workspace state: 8 workspaces, 96 entries per workspace, and 16 snapshots.
Replay gate: 512 log records and 64 segment boundaries before compaction must write a new checkpoint.
Over-limit write behavior: no truncation, eviction, implicit expansion, or partial persistence; callers must free space or move to a larger product envelope before retrying.
graduation_criteria: Keep the explicit product storage limits enforced in persistence gates or replace fixed tables with bounded dynamic allocation and quota enforcement.
Keep disk-chaos QEMU tests that write, reboot, interrupt, corrupt one slot, compact, and prove deterministic recovery.
Keep benchmark thresholds for storage replay, checkpoint compaction, workspace commit, file-bridge read, and memory pressure at target data sizes.
next_actions: Continue raising the bounded envelope only with matching quota, replay, format-evolution, corruption, QEMU durability, and benchmark evidence.

tracks.title: Boot, attestation, and base update trust chain
current_evidence: Freestanding boot records can be verified against signed artifact manifests and compared across native smoke boots.
Remote attestation refuses emulator-rooted measured state and requires a provisioned non-software root.

A/B base selection, rollback, post-activation health markers, and selector-derived power-cycle rollback proof are covered by host logic, QEMU smoke evidence before native-ready, and required real-hardware proof markers.

The native smoke target now includes negative QEMU runs that reject a tampered boot artifact manifest, direct bootloader-measurement digest mutation, direct kernel/userspace-image/policy/driver-set measurement tampering, and a rollback target whose slot measurement no longer verifies before the boot can reach native-ready.

The signature envelope and signing CLI support Ed25519 and a provider-backed production ML-DSA-65 FIPS 204 profile with full-size signature storage and fail-closed verification for unsupported formats; the former Ed25519+ML-DSA-65 hybrid preview commitment profile has been removed so no placeholder post-quantum path exists in the envelope.

A signature-provider boundary and registry now report provider profile, key custody, hardware-backed release eligibility, lifecycle controls, customer-verifier protocol, FIPS 204/FIPS 140 validation metadata, and fail-closed profile mismatches so production Ed25519 or validated ML-DSA providers can be swapped in without changing manifest storage layouts.

Attestation statements carry verifier-visible nonempty hardware root key ids and nonzero generations, verifier expectations can reject stale or revoked generations after provider rotation, and visible remote attestations now require fresh bounded challenge nonces with bounded replay-cache rejection before signing.

Remote attestation now has bounded verifier request and response records that bind nonce, remote party, visible policy label, expected key origin, root key id, minimum root generation, revoked root generations, and any required attestation verifier metadata digest to a request digest before signing or verification.

Attestation roots now have a production external-provider implementation that provisions key-handle metadata for TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or cloud-KMS custody, rejects local-software custody for production roots, requires verifier metadata digests for production providers, and verifies callback signatures against the provisioned public identity before issuing remote-attestation responses.

Production attestation descriptors now reject fake, mock, fixture, smoke, test-only, local-software, synthetic, or simulated operational names before provider metadata or external-provider initialization can treat a root as production eligible.

Platform-service and booted service-path attestation proofs now provision production external-provider key handles instead of test-only fake roots, require verifier metadata digests in the attestation challenge, and pin those digests into downstream network identity policy.

The NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof model now accepts attestation root lifecycle evidence only from real-target proofs that rotate to a higher root generation, propagate at least one revoked generation, reject stale and revoked root generations, bind the verifier metadata digest to the attestation challenge, and observe verifier rejection of stale attestations; unit tests reject QEMU, stale-rotation, missing-revocation, missing-stale-rejection, and missing-metadata-binding proofs, and the hardware proof bundle checker now requires both the emitted ATTESTATION_ROOT_LIFECYCLE marker and a structured attestation-lifecycle.txt sidecar with generation, revocation, rejection, metadata-digest, and request-digest evidence.

Release-signing and attestation external providers now emit verifier metadata records that own their public key bytes and bind provider name, key id, generation, custody boundary, lifecycle controls, verifier protocol, public key, and FIPS posture into a digest; host tests prove stale, local-software, validation-mismatched, or public-key-tampered metadata fails to match the provider, and release-security-check now runs negative keyring fixtures proving public-release keyrings are rejected unless active keys have configured dates, public keys, provider names, and verifier metadata digests.

Userspace package signatures, boot artifact manifest signatures, generated archive signatures, and attestation statement signatures now route through provider boundaries instead of directly selecting raw Ed25519 operations; the native smoke boot artifact manifest path uses a release-eligible provider fixture so smoke signing exercises key-handle based custody semantics.

Demo seed packages, SDK simulator release bundles, rendered-shell journeys, package-service fixtures, and spec release fixtures now select the Ed25519 provider explicitly where they model release signing behavior.

Package-service update gates now reject exact signed replay, active-version regression, publisher drift, update-channel drift, update-source drift, schema-version regression, empty install sources, oversized install source identities, and invalid data schema versions, including adversarial spec coverage for freshly signed downgrade metadata.

Installed package launch plans, resolved active manifests, and rollback targets now fail closed when the package publisher key has been revoked, so revocation blocks both future updates and already-installed code paths.
production_gaps: Host evidence still uses emulator-provided measurement fallbacks, and external-provider callbacks still route through software fixtures until real hardware or managed-key services are wired.

The provider, request/response, key-handle custody, rotation, revocation, and verifier protocol boundaries exist in source, but the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed root has not been provisioned on real hardware.

No local FIPS 204 ML-DSA implementation exists; the production path is the ml-dsa-65 external provider profile with FIPS validation metadata, and Ed25519 remains the only local signing profile until that provider is linked.

Release artifact signing, bootloader measurement handoff, and update rollback now have provider-bound smoke-level tamper rejection, selector-derived power-cycle rollback proof, and QEMU rollback markers, but they are not yet tied to a real TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS deployment or captured on real hardware.
graduation_criteria: Introduce a hardware-root abstraction that supports TPM and secure enclave backed quote/sign operations without exposing root seed material.
Add verifier-facing attestation request and response records with nonce, remote party, policy visibility, key rotation, and revocation tests.

Link an audited FIPS 204 ML-DSA provider through the external provider boundary, publish its validation certificate in the keyring, and move rollout from shadow to canary to required after verifier evidence passes.
Broaden release-image tamper gates from smoke fixtures to direct bootloader measurement mutation cases under operational signing keys.
next_actions: Wire the production root provider interface to the first supported TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS implementation and keep fake providers test-only.
Capture the attestation root lifecycle proof in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle after the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS root is provisioned.

Move explicit software-provider release fixtures onto operational Ed25519 plus ML-DSA key provisioning once the hardware-backed root, FIPS validation metadata, and release key-management interfaces exist.

Replace the release-eligible smoke signing fixture with the first operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed signing command and publish concrete verifier metadata digests from that provider.
Capture the update rollback marker group in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: First real hardware target: Intel NUC11TNKi5
current_evidence: The first supported hardware target is pinned to Intel NUC 11 Pro Kit NUC11TNKi5 instead of a generic PC-compatible bucket.

The target contract enumerates UEFI boot, ACPI tables, APIC timer, GOP framebuffer, USB xHCI input, NVMe block I/O, Intel I225-LM network, compositor framebuffer presentation, suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback power cycling as required hardware proof.
The build exposes an OVMF-backed uefi-qemu-test preflight for the ISO path before attempting the same image on the NUC firmware.

The Multiboot entry path now preserves bootloader magic and info pointers, asks GRUB to keep a 32-bit framebuffer payload, and exposes tested memory-map and framebuffer handoff parsers for runtime proof capture.
The kernel tree now has a tested SMBIOS scanner/parser that can match the NUC11TNKi5 SKU from real firmware tables before emitting real-hardware source or board markers.
The kernel tree now has a tested ACPI RSDP parser and aligned scanner as the first non-invasive ACPI building block for the target.
The ACPI parser now validates SDT headers and XSDT/RSDT root-table entries so the hardware proof path can require MADT and FADT presence instead of a standalone RSDP checksum.
The kernel tree now has a tested MADT parser that summarizes local APIC, I/O APIC, interrupt-source override, x2APIC, and PC-AT compatibility data before APIC timer bring-up.

The kernel tree now has a tested APIC timer interrupt proof that requires a valid LAPIC vector, nonzero divisor and initial count, count advancement, delivered timer interrupts, and EOI accounting, plus a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC APIC timer marker unless hardware LAPIC timer register writes, current-count reads, ISR vector observations, interrupt-handler entries, EOI register writes, and TSC advancement are present.

The kernel tree now has a tested FADT parser and ACPI suspend/resume proof model for PM control blocks, PM event blocks, SCI wake interrupts, PM timer advancement, reset plumbing, and resumed timer/framebuffer/xHCI/NVMe/I225 subsystem usability, plus a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC suspend/resume marker unless PM1 sleep writes, S-state entry observations, S0 resume observations, PM timer resume reads, SCI wake interrupts, and post-resume subsystem probes are present.

The kernel tree now has a tested UEFI GOP-style linear framebuffer descriptor validator with stride, buffer-size, pixel-format, and text-grid checks, plus a scanout proof that requires sampled framebuffer bytes to be nonblank and contain an expected rendered pixel, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC GOP framebuffer marker unless GOP mode-info reads, framebuffer base/stride observations, framebuffer memory-read bytes, display scanout observations, expected-pixel observations, captured scanline bytes, and sink-signal observations are present.

The native compositor framebuffer path now has a tested presentation proof with frame dimensions, byte counts, nonblank coverage, a content digest, active-window evidence, visible-window evidence, and expected rendered text before booted compositor markers are emitted.

The kernel tree now has a bounded crash-record format with checksum validation, redacted summary output, and executable persistence proof that validates recovered records across advanced boot ids, plus a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses the NUC crash recovery and persistence markers unless crash-handler entries, persistent record writes and flushes, reboot observations, recovery-boot reads, recovered-record validations, redacted report emissions, and persistent byte counts are present.
PCI inventory helpers now identify NVMe controllers and the Intel I225-LM network controller required by the NUC target.

The kernel tree now has a tested NVMe inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, admin-queue validation, fail-closed kernel data-plane transfer behavior, sector-aligned read/write completions, modeled MMIO queue doorbells, page-aligned PRP/DMA evidence, completion-head accounting, deterministic write/read cycle proof generation, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC storage markers unless controller-written completions, DMA read/write byte counts, interrupt evidence, and phase-tag observations are present.

The kernel tree now has a tested Intel I225-LM inventory shim with RX/TX ring-plan validation, fail-closed kernel transmit behavior, descriptor-backed software TX/RX completions, modeled MMIO tail-register writes, aligned packet-buffer evidence, PHY link-status evidence, interrupt-cause accounting, deterministic packet cycle proof generation, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC packet markers unless hardware-owned TX/RX descriptor evidence, DMA byte counts, asserted interrupts, and PHY packet observations are present.

The kernel tree now has a tested xHCI input inventory shim with controller-capability parsing, command/event ring validation, USB boot-keyboard descriptor enumeration, port connection, device-slot enable/address, configured interrupt-IN endpoint validation, modeled MMIO command and transfer doorbells, device/input/endpoint context-memory ownership evidence, ERST setup evidence, runtime event-ring counters, event-counted input delivery, fail-closed USB input report behavior, and a separate productionHardwareVerified path that refuses NUC keyboard markers unless hardware event TRBs, event-ring DMA writes, controller context reads, interrupt assertions, port-status changes, and input-report DMA bytes are present.

Production driver attachment now requires an explicitly detected, non-synthetic, target-grade device inventory record before minting driver authority, registering a device binding, or attaching a storage data plane as a production volume; device inventory starts every class absent with device_id=0 instead of stable synthetic defaults, kernel boot inventory captures Intel I225-LM, NVMe, and xHCI provenance through target-specific PCI helpers without seeding ATA bootstrap storage first, xHCI controller inventory seeds both USB-controller and input-device binding for the first target, PS/2 bootstrap input is rejected for production input binding, hosted modeled boots seed explicit I225-LM/NVMe/xHCI inventory records before production binding, and ATA bootstrap observations can no longer satisfy the production storage-driver binding or production storage-volume attachment for the NVMe-only first target.

A composed kernel hardware-proof module now gates NUC markers on real SKU evidence, Multiboot memory-map handoff, GOP hardware framebuffer scanout proof evidence, ACPI MADT/FADT discovery, APIC hardware LAPIC timer proof evidence, xHCI hardware event-ring input proof evidence, NVMe hardware-DMA write/read proof evidence, I225 hardware descriptor-ring packet proof evidence, hardware power-transition suspend/resume proof counts, hardware reboot-persistence crash-record proof counts, and hardware power-cycle update rollback proof counts.

The NUC11TNKi5 proof bundle contract now requires real-hardware source metadata, Jujutsu change/commit provenance, sidecar firmware settings, power-cycle notes, structured attestation lifecycle evidence, proof-window-bounded sidecar timestamps, artifact digests, all subsystem PASS markers, concrete SMBIOS/Multiboot/ACPI/APIC/GOP/xHCI/NVMe/I225/suspend/crash/update/attestation-lifecycle fact markers, observation-before-PASS marker ordering, all booted production-evidence markers including accelerator queue ownership and completion-interrupt markers, and minimum cold-boot, reboot, storage, network, suspend/resume, crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback counters.

Production readiness rejects QEMU-only evidence for this target; hardware proof requires captured real-machine logs, concrete device fact markers, firmware settings, power-cycle notes, booted service/sync/driver/compositor/permission/update markers, and repeated cold boot, reboot, suspend/resume, storage, network, crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback cycles.
production_gaps: The repo can now emit NUC11TNKi5 subsystem PASS markers and concrete hardware fact markers only when the corresponding firmware, device, and power-cycle facts are present, but no real NUC11TNKi5 boot log has been captured.
UEFI handoff still depends on the GRUB ISO path and has not been proven on the selected NUC firmware.

ACPI RSDP, XSDT/RSDT, MADT, APIC timer interrupt proof modeling, FADT discovery, and suspend/resume proof modeling are wired into proof capture; NUC APIC timer marker recording now rejects modeled-only LAPIC timer proof without hardware register/interrupt evidence, and NUC suspend/resume marker recording rejects modeled-only ACPI suspend proof without hardware power-transition evidence, but no real LAPIC timer interrupt run or suspend/resume cycle has been captured on the target hardware.

The framebuffer descriptor validator is wired to Multiboot/GOP-style framebuffer handoff, native compositor presentation is proof-gated in the modeled framebuffer, and the kernel GOP marker now rejects modeled-only framebuffer samples without hardware GOP scanout evidence, but real GOP ownership and rendering still need capture on HDMI/framebuffer output.

Crash record formatting and recovered-record persistence proof are tested, and NUC crash marker recording now rejects modeled-only persistence without hardware reboot-persistence evidence, but real crash records are not yet written before reboot or consumed by a recovery boot on the target hardware.

PCI target identification, NVMe controller queue validation, executable modeled NVMe MMIO doorbell/PRP completion proof cycles, and executable modeled I225 tail-register, interrupt, PHY-link, and TX/RX packet proof cycles are tested; NUC storage marker recording now rejects modeled-only NVMe completions without hardware-DMA evidence and NUC network marker recording rejects modeled-only I225 packet cycles without hardware descriptor-ring evidence, but real NVMe controller register writes, DMA ownership capture, hardware completions, Intel I225-LM descriptor-ring ownership, hardware interrupts, and PHY-backed packet I/O are not implemented.

xHCI capability parsing, ring validation, descriptor-level boot-keyboard enumeration, port/slot/address lifecycle, configured interrupt-transfer validation, modeled MMIO doorbell, context-memory, ERST, and event-ring proof, event-counted delivery, and boot-keyboard HID report handling are tested; NUC keyboard marker recording now rejects modeled-only xHCI input without hardware event-ring evidence, but real xHCI MMIO register writes, hardware-owned device contexts, and hardware event-ring input reports have not been captured from the controller.

Real suspend/resume, crash recovery, crash-record persistence, update rollback across physical power cycles, compositor framebuffer capture, and booted production-evidence marker capture need real-device implementations and logs; NUC update rollback marker recording now rejects modeled-only selector rollback without hardware power-cycle evidence.
graduation_criteria: Boot the NUC11TNKi5 from a UEFI USB image built from the repo and archive the serial/framebuffer proof bundle.
Emit and verify every marker in spec/hardware/nuc11tnki5-required-markers.txt from real hardware.
Pass the minimum cycle counts encoded by hardware_target.first_supported_target without panic, hang, unredacted crash data, update rollback loss, or persistence loss.
Keep QEMU smoke, storage durability, driver restart, sync two-node, recovery, and spec gates green before accepting hardware proof as production evidence.
next_actions: Make build/os.iso boot reliably through the NUC11TNKi5 UEFI firmware and record firmware settings.
Capture the new Multiboot memory-map, SMBIOS SKU, ACPI table, APIC hardware LAPIC timer interrupt-proof, and GOP hardware framebuffer scanout-proof markers from the NUC11TNKi5 firmware.
Use scripts/prepare-nuc11tnki5-hardware-proof.sh --build to create the proof manifest, sidecar templates, and artifact digest manifest before capture.

Feed real GOP mode-info reads, framebuffer base/stride observations, framebuffer memory-read bytes, display scanout observations, expected-pixel observations, captured scanline bytes, and sink-signal observations into the productionHardwareVerified framebuffer proof; feed real APIC timer initial-count/divide/LVT register writes, current-count reads, ISR vector observations, interrupt-handler entries, EOI register writes, and TSC advancement into the productionHardwareVerified timer proof; feed real suspend/resume PM1 sleep writes, S-state entry observations, S0 resume observations, PM timer resume reads, SCI wake interrupts, and post-resume subsystem probes into the productionHardwareVerified suspend proof; feed real crash-handler entries, persistent record writes and flushes, reboot observations, recovery-boot reads, recovered-record validations, redacted report emissions, and persistent byte counts into the productionHardwareVerified crash persistence proof; feed real update candidate activation writes, selector-record flushes, power-cycle observations, failure-detector observations, rollback decision records, stable-slot boot observations, recovered-slot reads, persisted-state verifications, and service-start suppression observations into the productionHardwareVerified update rollback proof; feed real xHCI MMIO command submission, hardware-owned device-slot and endpoint context reads, ERST/event-ring DMA writes, interrupt assertions, port-status changes, and boot-keyboard report DMA bytes into the productionHardwareVerified input proof; feed real NVMe doorbell/MMIO queue submission, DMA/PRP read/write byte counts, controller-written completions, interrupts, and phase-tag observations into the productionHardwareVerified storage proof; and feed real Intel I225-LM tail-register writes, hardware-owned TX/RX descriptors, DMA byte counts, asserted interrupts, and PHY packet observations into the productionHardwareVerified network proof before emitting PASS markers.
Add suspend/resume, induced crash-recovery, crash-record persistence, and update rollback power-cycle loops to the NUC proof runbook.
Capture service startup, compositor presentation-proof markers, permission review, sync, driver restart, crash persistence, and update rollback markers in the NUC proof run.

tracks.title: Userspace launch and service image provenance
current_evidence: The build generates a userspace image archive and production artifact manifest for freestanding boot profiles.
Launch provenance, component ABI metadata, signed bundle state, and syscall-dispatched task creation are enforced in native modules.
Negative tests reject unsigned userspace launches and modeled runtime bypasses.
The production-readiness gate rejects unmarked syntheticUserspaceImage fixtures in critical launch and service test paths; existing synthetic fixtures are marked model-only.

The catalog registration path now uses an arena-backed image table with a bundle secondary index, rejects metadata-only executable registration, and rejects generated userspace artifacts when embedded ELF bytes are missing or malformed, when precomputed digests no longer match, or when generated ELF metadata and manifest state become stale.

Boot-registered userspace images now preload from the generated userspace archive on host and freestanding builds; the boot registry rejects missing or unregistered generated artifacts, and registered launch paths refuse metadata-only catalog records for all launch bundles.

Rendered-shell task launch now resolves executable metadata from the generated userspace image archive by bundle id and fails closed outside model-only tests when a configured bundle lacks a generated image.
Compositor task-view checkpoint tests now persist and restore app-linked windows for generated archive-backed app tasks instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
OS contract process-isolation checks now create contract tasks from generated userspace image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors.
Host launch, service, syscall, storage, sync, and scheduler tests now use generated-image fixture readers for archive-backed executable descriptors in critical userspace paths.

The QEMU native smoke gate now requires generated userspace artifacts, scheduler binding, userspace exec/resume probes, service contract registration, service IPC connectivity, and driver restart markers before native-ready.
The service registry now rejects invalid bootstrap endpoints, zero binding identifiers, and unknown service connection flags before registering typed interfaces.

The secure pasteboard service is now generated as a userspace service image, launched through the kernel-contract service bootstrap path, published as a native service contract, and included in the service IPC connectivity proof loop.

Core manifest validation now rejects POSIX and compat.* bundle/component namespaces before application packaging, and the SDK linter delegates bundle/component compatibility checks to that manifest policy while keeping IDL text diagnostics.
production_gaps: Real-hardware proof still needs to capture the booted userspace startup and service IPC markers from the NUC11TNKi5.
graduation_criteria: Keep critical launch-path tests on fixtures derived from generated userspace image artifacts.
Keep bundle launch paths archive-backed on every build profile and reject metadata-only catalog entries for service, app, and session bundles.
Keep stale, truncated, unsigned, missing-byte, malformed-ELF, and digest-mismatched userspace archive tests in the spec and host gates.
Keep the QEMU service-startup proof exercising generated-image boot, mailbox, descriptor validation, syscall query, service IPC, fault, and restart paths before native-ready.
next_actions: Capture the service-startup marker group in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Booted permission review and policy mediation
current_evidence: Freestanding QEMU boots now run the permission review flow before native-ready using generated app packages, the permission review service task, compositor-backed review rendering, policy mediation, and explicit grant/deny markers.

Signed policy objects now live in an indexed arena with primary policy-id lookup and a scope multimap, so active-policy decisions and revocation avoid legacy first-free table scans while preserving signed generation ordering.

The booted permission proof now feeds every Notes, Sync, and Capture review command through the xHCI HID boot-keyboard report path without the bootstrap review profile, and the native smoke contract requires explicit xHCI keyboard report, review-command, and full boot-flow command markers.

Permission review service paths reject zero audit ticks, oversized scripted commands, and rendered-surface controls before the review window exists, so profiled review flows remain bounded and auditable.

The native smoke marker contract requires review-port readiness, policy-port readiness, rendered review output, zero-authority denials, local grants, explicit device/media decisions, and lease expiry evidence.
The NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof marker file requires the same permission review and xHCI keyboard full-flow markers from real hardware serial output.
production_gaps: The booted permission proof is QEMU-backed; the first real hardware proof bundle has not captured the same markers yet.
graduation_criteria: Keep permission review markers release-gated in QEMU before native-ready and require the same markers in the hardware proof bundle.
Require real hardware input events from the NUC11TNKi5 xHCI path for at least one booted permission command before accepting the hardware proof bundle.
Reject hardware proof bundles that omit review rendering, grant, deny, and lease-expiry markers.
next_actions: Capture permission review and xHCI keyboard full-flow markers in build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/serial.log.

tracks.title: Live sync and private overlay transport
current_evidence: Sync state covers device graph enrollment, durable inbound/outbound frame queues, replay rejection, selective policy, per-object sharing, CRDT merge semantics, secret transfer markers, transactional database contracts, and explicit conflict review/resolution.

SyncService now rebuilds resident workspace-policy, overlay, database-contract, conflict, and transport-frame path indexes from persisted state on startup, then services selective-policy, overlay, transactional-contract id, bundle, equivalence, conflict review, and latest-frame-by-path lookups through keyed indexes instead of scanning fixed persistent arrays.

The overlay relay service rejects unauthorized relay use, target changes, empty encrypted packets, malformed zero-tick/zero-task egress requests, and relay fallback re-checks revoked device trust before enqueueing failed native sends across both disconnected/congested and post-send network-failure paths.

Native sync transport ABI host tests now bind captured frames to source and target task ids, require payload digests on the wire, reject zero or malformed frame headers, reject non-device or same-device endpoints, enforce packet/session metadata before encoding, reject invalid task ids before endpoint allocation, preflight packet-capture capacity before endpoint or driver side effects, and fail closed on mutated encrypted packet metadata during decrypt.

End-to-end host tests replicate document, media, secret, and database payloads between two service tasks through a booted relay fallback model, and prove object-scoped grants skip private entries while offline conflicts stay reviewable.

The two-node QEMU gate boots separate native nodes with separate native-store images and now requires booted device graph, policy, device-to-device, relay, revoked-device, persisted sync-service restart, and native driver packet-capture markers on each node.

The booted sync scenario sends encrypted native transport ABI frames through network_driver_task.sendActiveFrame, validates the captured packet equals the active driver's transmitted frame, rejects plaintext-on-wire evidence, and requires packet-captured/frame-sent, malformed-packet rejection, reconnect, replay-window rejection, and congestion-backpressure markers before native-ready.

NativeTransportService now has a production fail-closed mode that refuses endpoint delivery, packet capture, and active-driver transmit until a real Intel I225 proof with ring ownership, PHY link, tail-register writes, interrupts, MAC evidence, and the first-target network frame cycle count is attached.

TransportSession now records an explicit trust posture: relay/local-lab sessions remain local_lab_only, pinned service-identity sessions become production_attested only when verified remote attestation includes request-bound verifier metadata, and session key derivation binds the posture so lab and production sessions cannot share the same crypto context silently.

Network policy and transport session posture now require verified remote-attestation evidence with a bound verifier request digest and bound attestation verifier metadata digest before treating a pinned connection as production-attested; loose attested=true claims and root-pinned attestations without verifier metadata remain local-lab or denied for production policies.

NativeTransportService now exposes a typed verified service-identity open path that consumes the attestation response/request, measured boot record, trusted root, and policy-pinned attestation verifier metadata digest directly; the production regression uses that path and proves a response for the wrong service identity cannot open a production session.

The native network-driver service-identity path now carries verified-attestation state, the verifier request digest, and the request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest through connection creation, key derivation, frame metadata, and brokered transmit rechecks, with regression coverage proving brokered sends keep the same verified evidence instead of downgrading to loose attested flags.

The booted sync service-path proof now provisions its network identity root through the production external-provider boundary, requires a request-bound verifier metadata digest, and persists that digest into the service-identity network policy.

NativeTransportService can now require production-attested sessions before endpoint delivery, object-share encryption, packet capture, relay fallback, or active-driver transmit; the regression gate proves local-lab relay sessions stay blocked even after I225 hardware proof while pinned attested service-identity sessions can transmit.

The rendered production journey now surfaces the object-scoped trusted-overlay share grant and drives a real offline document conflict through sync conflict review/resolution, so object sharing and conflict handling are user-visible daily-driver evidence rather than backend-only sync assertions.
production_gaps: The booted QEMU proof now observes native driver packet capture, transmit ownership, replay-window rejection, reconnect, congestion backpressure, malformed captured-packet rejection, and production-mode I225 proof enforcement, but it still uses the modeled boot network device rather than real Intel I225-LM frame receive/transmit rings.
Real-hardware evidence still needs to capture the same sync markers on the NUC11TNKi5 with the Intel I225-LM path active and packet counters tied to physical frames.

Remote device identity sessions are explicitly marked local-lab unless pinned verified attestation-response evidence with a verifier request digest and request-bound attestation verifier metadata digest is present, but production-grade remote trust still depends on the boot/attestation track wiring external providers to operational TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS roots.
graduation_criteria: Replace sync_transport_harness as the primary evidence with a native transport service that runs through endpoint syscalls and the network driver task.
Keep the two-node QEMU replication gate covering offline policy, device-to-device replication, relay fallback, revoked-device rejection, and persisted restart before release.
Bind production remote device sessions to operational attestation roots while keeping local-lab sessions explicitly labeled and rejectable by production-only callers.
next_actions: Replace the modeled boot network device in the two-node sync proof with a QEMU-visible async NIC path that owns receive/transmit rings and packet counters.
Replace external-provider software callback fixtures for production remote sessions with provisioned TPM, secure-enclave, HSM, or KMS-backed attestation roots.

tracks.title: Notes and docs daily-driver slice
current_evidence: The rendered-shell production journey is now scoped to one Notes app daily-driver path rather than a generic desktop expansion path.

The journey installs a signed native Notes package, starts its native component, opens a notes workspace and document, reviews the local object-access permission, grants an object-scoped collaborative share, syncs only after sharing, updates and rolls back the package, recovers shell/runtime state, removes the package, and revokes device and policy authority.
The share step writes a concrete trusted-overlay, object-scoped workspace grant and verifies the collaborator can read and write the shared note before sync proceeds.

The production journey surface now renders the object-scoped share proof, records the share expiry and object id, creates a conflicting paired-device replica before sync, opens a sync-conflict review surface, resolves the conflict with the local document version, and keeps that conflict-review evidence in the final journey transcript.

Task-flow ledger evidence now includes share_document alongside install_app, open_workspace, open_document, review_permission_request, sync_workspace, update_app, rollback_app_update, recover_system, and remove_app.

The package-service lifecycle used by the journey now requires nonempty bounded install sources, nonzero monotonic data schema versions, monotonic active updates, stable publisher identity, stable update channels, and stable update sources before an installed Notes package can be replaced.

The Notes production journey now resolves install and update requests from a public store channel release catalog whose exact release, trusted-publisher, and bundle-to-release indexes cover exact version, latest/next, and version-regression checks. The channel refuses unsigned, signature-tampered, untrusted-publisher, or publisher-key-revoked releases; re-checks current publisher trust before resolving already-published releases; requires every published release to advance an append-only transparency sequence rooted in the previous channel root; rejects stale-root, forged-root, skipped-sequence, and per-bundle version-regression releases; carries that transparency sequence/root/log-head into package install requests, stored revisions, package launch-plan provenance, the launched task's runtime provenance record, the task debug provenance trail, and SDK debugger events/export text; records structured source fingerprints, transparency sequence, and root/log-head fingerprints on launch provenance events while keeping full roots on task launch state; rejects public-store installs without transparency evidence; rejects public-store updates that replay an already-installed sequence even after rollback; refuses launch, manifest resolution, and rollback when stored public-store transparency evidence has been stripped; exposes signed revision provenance, source identity, schema version, permission digest, signature metadata, and public-store transparency sequence to launch consumers; rejects releases without complete canonical SHA-256 supply-chain metadata; rejects releases without canonical SHA-256 asset digests and byte sizes; and rejects asset catalogs that do not match the signed manifest before producing the package install request.

The host journey now renders an ordered Notes daily-driver marker contract directly in the production journey surface for install/open, edit persistence, share/sync, update rollback, recovery/removal, authority revocation, and complete-path proof; the same marker set is required by the native-smoke cold-boot registry and the NUC11TNKi5 hardware marker contract.

The booted QEMU native smoke path now runs the ordered Notes daily-driver production journey through store:zigos/public before native-ready and emits the complete marker group on cold boot and cold reboot.

The booted shell input loop now renders typed document text, syncs the edited note, recovers runtime state while preserving the edit, and then continues through rollback, recovery, and package removal.

The bootstrapped native secure pasteboard service now replaces ambient clipboard assumptions with destination-bound, foreground-session-bound, user-gesture-bound, strictly expiring, read-once or revocable paste grants; audit events count pasteboard access and denials while redacting copied content from user-visible diagnostics.

The QEMU native smoke path now drives the booted Notes shell input loop with real text input, verifies the object-store payload equals the typed note, syncs that version device-to-device, recovers the shell/runtime checkpoint, and requires typed edit, typed sync, typed recovery, and typed-loop-complete markers before native-ready.
production_gaps: The ordered Notes daily-driver marker path and typed editor loop are now emitted by booted QEMU native smoke, but the complete path has not yet been captured on real hardware.
graduation_criteria: Keep the first daily-driver scenario narrow: Notes app install, notes workspace/document use, explicit permission review, object-scoped sharing, local-first sync, update rollback, recovery, and package removal.
Keep the ordered Notes daily-driver marker path required by QEMU native smoke before broadening desktop surface area.
Require the same journey markers in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle before calling the slice production-ready.
next_actions: Capture the complete Notes daily-driver marker group in build/hardware-proofs/nuc11tnki5/serial.log.

tracks.title: Userspace driver data-plane depth
current_evidence: Driver registration checks signed bundles, device-class authority, DMA range metadata, restart generations, and a constrained first target of brokered storage DMA domains: window-confined NVMe bus mastering, never unconfined bus-master DMA.

The device broker now indexes controller slots and programmed DMA domains by device using arena/index-backed tables; unconfined bus mastering is rejected, and bus mastering is accepted only as a brokered-buffer program whose declared windows enumerate the exact queue or bounce frames the real NVMe engine may touch.
Storage driver tasks attach through the kernel device broker; brokered bootstrap and published target-NVMe backends both export checked read/write bridges for freestanding volume access.

The driver boundary spec gate exercises brokered bootstrap read/write I/O, programs an IOMMU-style DMA domain, authorizes brokered DMA buffers, and rejects stale task authority, stale DMA buffers, stale broker sessions, expired leases, invalid ports, explicit broker revocation, and post-restart target generation mismatches.

The storage data-plane gate covers active-I/O restart, invalid-transfer propagation, and partial-transfer rejection across brokered bootstrap sessions and published NVMe backends before a restarted userspace driver reissues I/O.

The native network driver path reauthorizes brokered service-identity sends through the egress broker, so revoked network-policy capabilities stop already-open userspace network paths before transmit; network activation now fails closed until the published transport device id matches detected production Intel I225-LM inventory, and the booted sync path captures an encrypted native transport ABI frame that matches the active network driver transmit.

Driver broker, runtime lease, storage-driver attach, and driver-boundary spec tests now create runnable driver/control/app tasks from generated userspace image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors, and the production-readiness gate rejects synthetic descriptors in those driver data-path sources.

A native accelerator driver task now owns brokered GPU, NPU, and media queue sessions, requires hardware queue ownership plus completion-interrupt evidence, emits typed scheduler queue events only after rejecting CPU engines, missing brokers, missing owners, missing generations, missing interrupts, and stale completions, and the booted driver proof now emits queue-owned and completion-interrupt markers required by native smoke and the NUC11TNKi5 hardware marker contract.

QEMU driver restart proof performs storage reads and writes before and after restart, accepts published NVMe data-plane recovery as well as brokered bootstrap recovery, rejects invalid or partial transfers before port I/O, rejects stale access after deactivation, then gates republish/rebind before post-restart I/O; the expanded marker group is now required by the real-hardware proof marker contract.
production_gaps: Bootstrap storage has the deepest hardware-like data-plane proof; network now has booted encrypted frame ownership evidence and accelerator queues now have brokered driver-event evidence, but other driver classes remain inventory, policy, or publication proofs.
IOMMU and DMA isolation now have executable native programming and brokered-buffer evidence, but not real VT-d/AMD-Vi page-table programming or device fault capture.

QEMU coverage now gates brokered restart, timeout propagation, partial-sector rejection, explicit broker revocation, republish, and rebind; real hardware packet/block I/O evidence and mid-transfer device-fault capture are still pending.
graduation_criteria: Add broker-mediated data-plane tests for at least storage and network that run in QEMU and prove no kernel direct publication for excluded subsystems.
Replace the native IOMMU model with real hardware programming and fault evidence before broadening the first production target beyond brokered programmed-I/O storage.

Keep unconfined bus-master DMA fail-closed, and keep confined bus-master programs (the NVMe queue/bounce windows) modeled-evidence-only, until hardware IOMMU programming, queued invalidation, interrupt remapping, and captured device-fault records are present in the hardware proof bundle.
Gate driver restart on active I/O recovery, broker revocation, rebind, and no stale DMA or port access after generation change.
next_actions: Capture hardware packet/block I/O traces for timeout, mid-transfer fault, and post-restart recovery on the first production target.
Bind the native DMA-domain model, including the confined NVMe bus-master windows, to real VT-d/AMD-Vi programming and archive device-fault evidence before treating DMA isolation as hardware-enforced.
Capture the expanded driver restart/rebind marker group, including DMA-domain and brokered-buffer markers, in the NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof bundle.

tracks.title: Resource scheduler and live platform telemetry
current_evidence: Scheduler decisions account for resource class, engine availability, thermal pressure, battery saver, privacy mode, CPU budget, memory bandwidth, and zero-copy shared memory.
Booted provider tests derive hardware-source telemetry from live runtime counters instead of purely synthetic state.
Telemetry now flows through an explicit provider boundary with test-only host fakes and production freestanding provider descriptors.
Negative tests require complete hardware telemetry before waking hardware queues.

Scheduler host tests now create runnable task records from generated userspace image fixtures, so dispatch, throttling, and fairness checks exercise archive-backed executable metadata instead of synthetic image descriptors.

The OS contract now treats background activity as a first-class native policy surface, and the dispatcher enforces signed duration, CPU, memory, remote-network, visibility, typed-service, overdue-work expiration, reservation release, and redacted-diagnostics gates before and after reserving work.

Media/print helper jobs now use an indexed arena for primary job lookup/allocation, keep completed job records addressable without linear scans, and reject full job tables before taking scheduler accelerator claims.

The notification center now stores notifications in an indexed arena with primary-id lookup plus a source/reason multimap for replacement suppression, maintains non-expiring attention counts directly, keeps expiring notices in a small index, and maintains a visible-notification order chain so latest-visible, dismiss, suppression, and attention-budget checks avoid unrelated table scans.

Sensitive capture sessions now keep active-session and active-kind indexes alongside active/privacy-indicator counters, so active-at-tick and privacy-indicator-at-tick checks walk only live capture sessions and remove entries on explicit stop or lease expiry.

The agent delegation service now indexes active delegations by generation and tracks active generation buckets, so kill-switch revocation visits stale generations directly and refreshes the lowest active generation without rescanning delegation slots.

A sustained-load scheduler regression gate keeps foreground work continuously ready while proving background and batch classes still dispatch within bounded deadline windows without missed lower-class deadlines.
Expired lower-class deadline ties now break by service debt, so a repeatedly serviced background queue cannot hide an equally urgent batch queue.

Hardware telemetry samples now carry explicit reader evidence, and scheduler accelerator wake/claim paths refuse `.hardware` GPU, NPU, or media availability until ACPI, thermal, battery, accelerator-reader, target-id, and reader-generation evidence is complete.

Platform policy signal tests now derive booted runtime telemetry counters from generated userspace image fixture tasks instead of synthetic executable descriptors, and production readiness rejects reintroducing synthetic descriptors in that telemetry source.
OS contract resource-governance checks now create foreground, background, batch, and emergency tasks from generated userspace app/service image fixtures instead of synthetic executable descriptors.

The background dispatcher now records bounded activity history in an indexed arena, completes records by primary id lookup, keeps running records in an active index for overdue expiry, keeps completed/delayed/denied/expired records in a reusable index for bounded history replacement, tracks the latest record id directly, and maintains active dispatch counts for throttling without rescanning the record table.
Task runtime address spaces now use an indexed arena alongside task records, so launch, lookup, snapshot restore, and rehost replacement paths no longer maintain a separate manual id-index table.

QEMU benchmark checkpoint and scheduler-load tasks now pre-validate generated userspace app/service image fixtures and copy those archive-backed executable specs into benchmark task records instead of synthetic executable descriptors.

The first-target platform telemetry provider validates NUC11TNKi5 real-hardware reader snapshots before publishing hardware scheduler samples, rejects QEMU or incomplete reader evidence, and host tests prove partial hardware telemetry cannot grant accelerator work.

First-target telemetry snapshots can now be composed only from typed ACPI/FADT, thermal-zone, battery, and accelerator reader proofs with matching reader generations; tests reject QEMU ACPI proofs, stale thermal generations, online accelerator drivers without generations, and out-of-range thermal readings before scheduler hardware availability is published.

A first-target reader-provider boundary now binds provider role, target id, reader generation, and typed ACPI/thermal/battery/accelerator callbacks before telemetry counters can reach the scheduler; host tests reject test-only providers, target-mismatched proofs, and stale provider generations.

A concrete first-target driver callback provider now accepts raw ACPI/FADT, thermal-zone, battery, and accelerator samples, converts them into typed reader proofs, and fails closed when required callbacks are missing or samples are stale before booted scheduler telemetry is published.

The kernel hardware-proof state now retains parsed FADT firmware, boot memory capacity, thermal-zone samples, battery status, accelerator driver generations, and completion-interrupt observations under one reader generation; the native first-target adapter feeds those proof facts into the production driver callback provider and rejects missing FADT or memory evidence.

A first-target hardware telemetry driver recorder now validates thermal-zone, battery, GPU, NPU, and media driver readings against the ACPI/FADT telemetry base before calling the kernel proof recorders; host tests reject missing base proof, overheated sensors, missing battery devices, online accelerators without driver generations, and stale reader-generation updates.

The first-target telemetry recorder now has a boot/live source callback interface for independent thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon providers; tests prove missing battery or accelerator callbacks and malformed source readings fail closed before hardware proof facts update.

A first-target telemetry source registry now refuses to publish scheduler hardware telemetry until complete thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon callbacks are installed; host tests reject empty or incomplete registries before accepting installed source readings.

The first-target telemetry registry now exposes independent thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon provider slots while preserving complete-source publication semantics; host tests prove partial slot registration cannot update hardware proof facts or publish scheduler telemetry.

Captured NUC11TNKi5 hardware proof facts can now be installed through the production first-target telemetry provider slots; kernel and native tests reject missing thermal, battery, accelerator, memory, FADT, grid-carbon, and callback evidence before scheduler hardware telemetry is published.

First-target telemetry now rejects replayed same-generation thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon source sample sequences in the kernel recorder, and the native platform telemetry provider refuses same-generation reader snapshots unless every source sequence advances before refreshing scheduler hardware availability.

Grid-carbon telemetry now uses sequenced reader proofs with bounded intensity values, and scheduler hardware evidence is incomplete until ACPI, thermal, battery, accelerator, and grid-carbon observations are all present.

Userspace scheduler hardware-queue grants now require `.hardware` telemetry with complete reader evidence; emulator and synthetic telemetry can model policy but cannot wake GPU, NPU, or media queue claims, accelerator claims keep a per-engine deadline head for constant-time expired-deadline grants and a per-task claim index for duplicate/revocation paths, and low-level accelerator controllers expose an explicit production hardware-telemetry gate for direct callers.
